what_it_is.value: GPU terminal emulator whose author wrote the Kitty graphics protocol (APC G), the de facto modern way for programs to put raster images and animations into a terminal. It also ships kittens (icat displays images; hints labels paths and URLs) and open-actions, which decide what happens when you click a file or hyperlink.
what_it_is.note: [measured] Read the graphics-protocol, icat, hints and open_actions pages on 2026-09-24.

language.value: Python, C, Go, Objective-C (bytes: Python 3.44M, C 2.56M, Go 2.12M, ObjC 0.44M)
language.note: [measured] Kittens (icat, hints) are Go; the core and renderer are C and Python.

graphics_mechanism.value: Kitty graphics protocol, which kitty defines and hosts: APC `ESC _G<k=v,...>;<base64>ESC \`. Image data arrives by one of four transmission mediums: direct in the escape (t=d), a file path (t=f), a temp file (t=t) or POSIX shared memory (t=s). Images are uploaded once by id and then placed as placements with z-index; negative z draws under text, and below INT32_MIN/2 also under non-default cell backgrounds. Also supported: relative placements (P=/Q= parent), client- and terminal-driven animation (a=f frames, since 0.20.0), and Unicode placeholders, where the codepoint U+10EEEE carries the image id in its foreground colour and diacritics carry the row and column, so images survive tmux and vim. kitty has no Sixel support. Rendering is native OpenGL textures.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] All mechanism details come from the spec page. The spec page does not mention Sixel at all, so 'no Sixel' is general knowledge rather than a quoted statement.

where_it_draws.value: Protocol images draw as cell-anchored overlays inline in the scrollback. The spec says the graphics should also scroll with the text, automatically. They layer above or below text by z-index, and after a placement the cursor moves right by the placement's columns and down by its rows unless C=1. Separately, clicked files can open in a kitty overlay window that covers the active window (`launch --type=overlay`), in a split (`--location=hsplit|vsplit|split`), in a tab, in an OS window, or in an os-panel (a desktop panel).
where_it_draws.note: [measured] Scroll behaviour and z rules come from graphics-protocol; launch types come from the launch page.

input_model.value: Protocol images are inert pixels and receive no input. Ctrl+Shift+click on a hyperlink runs the first matching rule in open-actions.conf. Criteria are protocol, mime, ext, file glob, url regex and fragment_matches, and ${FILE_PATH}, ${URL} and ${FILE} are substituted into the action. An overlay window takes keyboard focus and returns it to the window beneath when it closes. The hints kitten (ctrl+shift+e for URLs, ctrl+shift+p then f for paths) is keyboard label selection. --program decides the result: paste it (-), copy it (@), use the default opener, or `launch` it.
input_model.note: [measured] open_actions example read verbatim: `protocol file / mime image/* / action launch --type=overlay kitten icat --hold -- ${FILE_PATH}`.

td_overlap.note: [measured] open-actions is click-to-open. Launching icat into an overlay or split is content in a pane. It is the reference host for the protocol TD would implement. It is not same-stack (C, Python and Go).

steal_for_td.value: Copy kitty's open-actions table as TD's Ctrl+click router. It is an ordered, first-match-wins list of rules. Each rule has criteria (protocol, mime, ext, file glob, url regex) and an action with ${FILE_PATH}, ${URL} and ${FILE} substituted. Ship defaults along these lines: image/* opens a floating square in the current pane; text/markdown and text/html open a split-pane viewer; anything else goes to xdg-open. TD's actions are its own pane types rather than kitty's `launch --type=overlay`, but the rule grammar, the ordering and the substitution variables transfer unchanged, and a user who knows kitty can already write TD rules.
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] Analysis over the open_actions page, which says processing stops at the first match.

trap.value: The file and shared-memory transmission mediums (t=f, t=t, t=s) come with mandatory security rules. The terminal must refuse device, socket and other special files, and may refuse /proc, /sys and /dev. It may delete a temp file only when it sits in a known temp dir and its path contains `tty-graphics-protocol`. And every file-access failure must return an identical error, so a remote or sandboxed client cannot learn which files exist. Start TD with t=d (direct) only. Add t=f, t=t and t=s later, and only with these rules implemented and tested.
trap.note: [inferred] The rules are quoted from the spec; the advice to stage them after direct transmission is my analysis.

what_it_is.value: Cross-platform GPU terminal emulator and multiplexer in Rust, configured in Lua. It lets programs draw images through the iTerm2 inline-image protocol (with a built-in `wezterm imgcat`), Sixel and a partial Kitty graphics implementation.
what_it_is.note: [measured] features.md lists: iTerm2 compatible image protocol support with imgcat; Kitty graphics support; Sixel graphics support (experimental, since 20200620-160318-e00b076c).

language.value: Rust (15.6M bytes), plus Python, Shell and Nix

graphics_mechanism.value: Three host protocols: iTerm2 OSC 1337 (since 20220319-142410-0fcdea07), Sixel (experimental) and Kitty APC G, which the code enables by default (`enable_kitty_graphics` defaults to true). All three decode into one shared cell model, `wezterm_cell::image::ImageCell`, which holds texture coordinates, a z_index and padding, and the GPU renderer allocates quads from it. The Kitty support has gaps. Tracking issue #986 leaves these unchecked: animation control, shared-memory transmission and Unicode placeholders (PR #7924 is still open).

where_it_draws.value: Images draw inline in scrollback, attached to terminal cells, so they scroll with text. Negative z_index draws under the text layer. #986 notes that wezterm maps Kitty placements onto cells at placement time, whereas the spec models them independently of cells. imgcat does not fully work through wezterm's own multiplexer sessions.
where_it_draws.note: [measured] image.rs doc comment: negative z_index renders beneath the text layer, and below INT32_MIN/2 it draws under cells with a background. The multiplexer caveat is from imgcat.html.

input_model.value: Images are inert. By default a plain left-click release runs CompleteSelectionOrOpenLinkAtMouseCursor, so clicking a matched link opens it. When a program has grabbed the mouse, holding Shift bypasses the grab (configurable via bypass_mouse_reporting_modifiers). Which text counts as a link is decided by hyperlink_rules (regex, format and highlight). Clicks can be rerouted in Lua through the `open-uri` event, for example to SpawnCommandInNewWindow; returning false suppresses the default browser open. Quick Select (Ctrl+Shift+Space) is a keyboard label mode over URLs, paths and hashes, drawn in the pane itself.

Image bytes are capped per screen by `image-storage-limit`, default 320 MB and separate for the primary and alternate screens; setting it to 0 disables all image protocols. trap.value: Multi-terminal image bookkeeping is where Rio broke. Its July 2026 graphics fixes are all state-lifetime bugs: image store keys were not scoped per terminal (#1752), GPU textures were not evicted when their pixels were freed (#1755), byte accounting drifted (#1756), and on Vulkan only one of two image layers drew (#1761). TD has many panes and a client/server split, so key every image by session or pane and tie GPU texture lifetime to the store entry.

what_it_is.value: Modern C++/Qt terminal with the widest image-protocol coverage in this cluster. It has Sixel, ReGIS vector graphics, Kitty graphics (added in 0.7.0), iTerm2 inline images, and its own experimental Good Image Protocol (GIP). Since 0.7.0 it also has tabs, splits and a daemon mode whose sessions outlive the window.

The experimental GIP is DCS-based with u/r/s/d operations: upload, render, upload-and-render, release. It has named image pools with LRU eviction, three compositing layers (below, replace, above), resize and alignment policies, and advertises itself as DA1 code 90; `contour cat` displays a file through it. Kitty animation (a=f/a=a/a=c) is still an open PR, #2109.

TD already splits client and server (the host owns the Term), so decoded image stores and placements belong on the host side of that split and should be replayed to a client that reconnects. The client should hold only GPU textures, which it can rebuild.

graphics_mechanism.value: OSC 1337: `ESC ] 1337 ; File=[args] : <base64> ^G`. Arguments are name (base64), size, width and height (N cells, Npx, N% or auto), preserveAspectRatio and inline (1 displays the file, 0 downloads it). Since 3.5 there is a multipart form, MultipartFile, then FilePart chunks, then FileEnd, which avoids tmux size limits. Animated GIFs have been supported since 2.9.20150512. Kitty APC G is also supported, handled by KittyImageController.swift. Sixel DCS goes through libsixel, decoded in the sandboxed process `iTerm2SandboxedWorker`.

input_model.value: Images are inert. Cmd-click runs Semantic History, configured per profile. The per-line working directory, tracked by shell integration, is what resolves relative paths.

updates.label: Alacritty (upstream) — the engine TD runs on, and why it refuses images
updates.group: B · Terminals that draw pixels for programs

what_it_is.value: Minimal OpenGL terminal whose `alacritty_terminal` crate is TD's VT engine. Upstream deliberately has no image protocol. Issue #910 (open since 2017, 225 comments) and ayosec's PR #4763 (open since 2021, 255 comments) are kept open but will not be merged. Maintainer Christian Duerr: 'This PR not being merged is all about image protocols being bad, not about maintainers not having time.'
what_it_is.note: [measured] Maintainer comments pulled via gh api. Further quotes: 'a massive patch for a mediocre protocol' (2024-05-28); 'Opting out of performance is not something that aligns with Alacritty's goals' (2024-05-28); 'this has little chance of ever getting upstreamed... There's nothing wrong with alternative Alacritty distributions' (2025-08-29).

language.value: Rust (1.14M bytes), plus Shell, GLSL and Makefile

graphics_mechanism.value: None for programs. The parser throws the bytes away before any handler sees them. Upstream `vte` routes ESC _ (APC, which Kitty uses) into `State::SosPmApcString`, where the bytes are ignored. The ansi Handler's DCS `hook`/`put` are '[unhandled hook]' debug stubs, so Sixel (DCS q) never arrives either. What exists is pixel-size reporting: `WindowSize` carries cell_width and cell_height, which fill TIOCSWINSZ ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel, and `Event::TextAreaSizeRequest` answers CSI 14 t.

updates.label: ayosec/alacritty 'graphics' — Sixel inside alacritty_terminal
updates.group: B · Terminals that draw pixels for programs

what_it_is.value: A long-maintained Alacritty fork (default branch `graphics`) that adds Sixel. Crucially for TD, the protocol state lives in the alacritty_terminal crate itself: a new graphics module, a per-cell graphics field and Term hooks. Only the OpenGL drawing sits in the alacritty binary crate. Upstream keeps the matching PR #4763 open as a pointer 'because ayosec has demonstrated to be a responsible maintainer of this patch set'.
what_it_is.note: [measured] The compare API shows 85 commits ahead and 17 behind upstream master. alacritty_terminal changes: graphics/mod.rs +666, graphics/sixel.rs +809, term/mod.rs +105/-1, term/cell.rs +34/-1, grid/mod.rs +12, grid/row.rs +6/-2, Cargo.toml +2/-1 (vte swap), lib.rs +1, plus sixel test fixtures. Renderer changes in the alacritty crate: renderer/graphics/{mod,draw,shader}.rs about 800 lines plus two GLSL shaders.

language.value: Rust (1.23M bytes), plus Shell, GLSL and Makefile

graphics_mechanism.value: Sixel only; docs/features.md says 'up to 1024 colors... limited to 4096x4096 pixels'. It swaps `vte` for the `vte-graphics` 0.15.0 crate (described as 'vte fork for the Alacritty's graphics patch') so DCS q reaches the Handler. `Graphics` on Term keeps a pending Vec<GraphicData> of RGB or RGBA pixels. Each covered cell gets a `GraphicCell` holding an Arc<TextureRef> plus x/y offsets. Drop impls push Remove or ClearSubregion ops into a shared queue, and the renderer drains everything with `Graphics::take_queues() -> Option<UpdateQueues { pending, remove_queue, clear_subregions }>`. It also answers XTSMGRAPHICS (`CSI ? Pi ; Pa ; Pv S`) and handles the shared or private Sixel palette.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Read graphics/mod.rs lines 1-514 and alacritty_terminal/Cargo.toml line 27: `vte = { version = "0.15.0", package = "vte-graphics", ... }`.

where_it_draws.value: Images draw inline and are attached to grid cells, so they scroll with text into scrollback and are freed when those cells are overwritten or dropped. With Sixel display mode set (DECSDM, TermMode::SIXEL_DISPLAY) an image starts at (0,0), the grid never scrolls and the cursor stays put.

input_model.value: Same as upstream Alacritty: hints, selection and Shift to bypass mouse capture. Graphics are inert. Writing text over a graphic clears that subregion via ClearSubregion.

activity.note: [measured] Tracks each upstream release. vte-graphics was last updated on crates.io 2025-02-24.

td_overlap.note: [measured] It changes the exact crate TD uses.

steal_for_td.value: Reuse the fork's alacritty_terminal half and write only a gpui consumer. Vendor ayosec's alacritty_terminal (about 1.6k added lines, all in the crate TD already uses), take `vte-graphics`, and each frame in TD's gpui paint call `term.graphics.take_queues()`. Upload `pending` RGBA as gpui image textures keyed by GraphicId, drop the ones in `remove_queue`, and paint each visible `GraphicCell` as a sub-rectangle (offset_x, offset_y, cell size) of its texture. The Sixel decode, the palette, XTSMGRAPHICS and the grid bookkeeping all come for free; TD writes only the paint. The same TextureRef and GraphicCell model can then take a Kitty decoder, as ekollof's cosmic-term fork did in graphics/kitty.rs (1,511 lines).
steal_for_td.note: [inferred] Line counts are measured via the compare API. That the queue API maps cleanly onto gpui textures is inferred, not prototyped.

trap.value: Version skew and a forked parser. The fork's alacritty_terminal reports version 0.25.2-dev on the graphics branch while TD is on crates.io 0.26. It depends on vte-graphics, a single-maintainer fork last published 2025-02-24. It is Sixel-only, with no Kitty and no Unicode placeholders. Vendoring means owning every upstream rebase. Pin to a tag, keep the diff isolated to graphics/, cell.rs and term hooks, and run vtebench before and after, because the extra per-cell graphics field is exactly what upstream measured as a slowdown.
trap.note: [measured] Versions measured; the advice is inferred.

updates.label: xterm.js @xterm/addon-image — Sixel + iTerm2 IIP (+ partial Kitty) in the browser terminal
updates.group: B · Terminals that draw pixels for programs

what_it_is.value: Official xterm.js addon that gives any xterm.js-based terminal inline images. That covers the terminals in VS Code, Hyper and Wave, among others. It supports SIXEL, iTerm2's inline image protocol (IIP) and, as work in progress, Kitty's graphics protocol.
what_it_is.note: [measured] README: 'Supports SIXEL, iTerm's inline image protocol (IIP) and partially Kitty's terminal graphics prtocol (TGP)'. The list of host apps is from the brief and general knowledge, not re-verified.

license.note: [measured] The addon lives in the xterm.js monorepo.

language.value: TypeScript (3.36M bytes, whole monorepo), plus JavaScript, Shell and CSS

graphics_mechanism.value: The DOM or canvas implementation of three host protocols. The SIXEL decoder is streamed, with a palette up to 4096 registers, DECSET 80 scrolling control and XTSMGRAPHICS. IIP accepts PNG, JPEG, GIF, QOI, WEBP and AVIF, with the browser doing every decode except QOI. Kitty is marked WIP. The addon turns on CSI 14 t, 16 t and 18 t size reports by default. Images are split into per-cell tiles on a canvas layer. Limits: pixelLimit 16,777,216; sixelSizeLimit, iipSizeLimit and kittySizeLimit 32 MiB each; FIFO storageLimit 128 MB of unpacked RGBA.
graphics_mechanism.note: [measured] Option defaults read from the README's IImageAddonOptions block.

where_it_draws.value: Images draw inline in scrollback as buffer-cell tiles and scroll with text. Images on the alternate buffer are erased when the buffer switches. Evicted images that are still in scrollback show a placeholder pattern when showPlaceholder is true.

input_model.value: Images are inert to the user. The host app gets `getImageAtBufferCell(x, y)`, which returns the original, unresized image as a canvas for an absolute buffer position, and `extractTileAtBufferCell(x, y)`, which returns the single tile. With these a host app can build click-an-image-to-open itself.

activity.note: [measured] These are repository-level numbers; the addon has no separate repo.

td_overlap.note: [measured] TypeScript in the DOM, so not same-stack.

steal_for_td.value: Make an inline image clickable into TD's viewer. Give the terminal core a `image_at_cell(point)` that returns the original-resolution image behind any grid cell, as xterm.js's getImageAtBufferCell does. Ctrl+click on an inline Kitty or Sixel image then opens it in TD's floating square or split viewer at full size. That joins TD's two planned features, programs drawing pixels and click-to-open, into one gesture. Also borrow the eviction placeholder: an image evicted from storage but still in scrollback draws a hatch, not a blank.

trap.value: Image memory is per terminal instance and adds up. The addon's storageLimit is per Terminal, and the README tells embedders to lower it at runtime 'if you have multiple terminal instances running, that all add to one upper memory limit'. Its default is 128 MB of unpacked RGBA per instance. At TD's roughly 20 panes, per-pane defaults like that reach gigabytes, so the budget has to be global and each pane has to draw from it.
trap.note: [measured] The quote is from the Storage section; the pane arithmetic is mine.

bubbles.note: Neither image protocol can reach TD's alacritty_terminal Handler today. Upstream vte sends ESC _ (APC, used by Kitty's `ESC _G`) to State::SosPmApcString and discards the bytes (vte src/lib.rs line 379). The vte ansi Performer's DCS `hook`/`put`, which Sixel's `DCS q` needs, are debug-log stubs (src/ansi.rs line 1311). So TD has three options: (a) a patched vte, as ayosec's `vte-graphics` 0.15.0 does; (b) a byte pre-filter in front of the parser that extracts APC G and DCS q, which then needs the cursor position and must emit the cursor moves itself; or (c) a different core such as rio-vt, which parses both natively.
bubbles.why: This is the single fact that decides how much of the graphics work touches TD's VT dependency. No approach avoids a parser change.

bubbles.note: TD already answers pixel-geometry queries correctly. app/src/host.rs handles TermEvent::TextAreaSizeRequest by formatting WindowSize{num_lines, num_cols, cell_width: geom.cell_width, cell_height: geom.cell_height} and writing the reply to the PTY. alacritty_terminal also fills TIOCSWINSZ ws_xpixel/ws_ypixel from those same cell sizes (tty/unix.rs lines 431-435). Kitty, Sixel and IIP clients size images from these numbers, so this prerequisite is already done. The only 8x16 and 8x20 hard-codes are in the socketpty test and the term.rs bench.
bubbles.why: It removes one prerequisite from TD's image plan, and it shows the host (server) side owns geometry, which is where the image store should live too.

bubbles.note: Queries a Kitty-graphics host must answer: (1) a=q query: reply `ESC _Gi=<id>;OK ESC \`, or `ENOENT:<msg>` or another error code. It must reply immediately and must not store the image. (2) Detection: clients send `ESC _Gi=31,s=1,v=1,a=q,t=d,f=24;AAAA ESC \` followed by `ESC [c`; the graphics reply arriving before the DA1 reply means supported. (3) Quiet modes q=1 (suppress OK) and q=2 (suppress errors too). (4) After a placement the cursor moves right by cols and down by rows unless C=1. (5) When over quota, delete images that have no placements first. (6) Deletes via a=d with d=i/p/z etc.; uppercase also frees the data.
bubbles.why: This is the minimum surface for a=q-probing clients (yazi, chafa, timg, kitty icat, ratatui-image) to pick TD up as a Kitty host.

bubbles.note: Unicode placeholders are the multiplexer-safe form of the Kitty protocol. The program creates a virtual placement (a=p,U=1), then prints U+10EEEE cells whose foreground colour encodes the image id (256-colour or 24-bit, with a third diacritic carrying the most significant byte) and whose combining diacritics encode row and column (U+0305 = 0, U+030D = 1, and so on). Anything that treats them as text (tmux, vim, TD's own server/client mirror) repositions the image for free. Support today: Ghostty (graphics_unicode.zig), iTerm2 3.7 (a placeholder fix is in the 3.7 notes), Rio (#1891/#1893, fixed 2026-08-24), and the ekollof cosmic-term fork (rowcol_diacritics.rs). WezTerm does not have it yet (PR #7924 open).
bubbles.why: Because the image rides in ordinary cells, TD's grid, selection, scrollback and client/server mirroring already carry it. This is likely the cheapest correct first Kitty feature for a multiplexing terminal.

bubbles.note: Queries a Sixel host must answer, as implemented in the ayosec fork and xterm.js: advertise Sixel in DA1 (the VT220+ '4' attribute; chrisduerr notes '4' means nothing while Alacritty reports VT102). Answer XTSMGRAPHICS `CSI ? Pi ; Pa ; Pv S` for Pi=1 (colour registers, 1024 in the fork) and Pi=2 (Sixel geometry, capped at 4096x4096; the fork answers via TextAreaSizeRequest). Honour DECSDM (DECSET/DECRST 80, Sixel display or scrolling mode) and choose the shared or private palette mode. Also answer CSI 14 t, 16 t and 18 t pixel and char size reports.
bubbles.why: Sixel clients (chafa, notcurses, mpv vo=sixel, lsix) probe these before drawing. A missing or incorrect reply makes them fall back to half-block characters.

bubbles.note: Rio's maintainer opened zed-industries/zed PR #62149 on 2026-08-04, 'terminal: Replace alacritty_terminal with rio-vt'. It swaps Zed's (gpui) terminal core through the existing seam in crates/terminal/src/alacritty.rs, now rio.rs, keeping the public Cell, Content, Modes and Point shapes so that nine dependent crates compile untouched. It claims 2-8x parse throughput over alacritty_terminal 0.26 (maintainer's own benchmark, self-disclosed as an interested party). A Zed member (mikayla-maki) closed it the same day: 'we're not able to field this kind of PR'.
bubbles.why: This is a same-stack (gpui) precedent for replacing alacritty_terminal with an image-capable core, and the diff maps the API differences TD would hit. The throughput numbers are unverified.

bubbles.note: Zed's position on terminal images (for cluster A's zed-terminal row): issue #20860 'Graphics support in the integrated terminal' was closed with 'Zed uses Alacritty and does not modify it in any way, esp. related to graphics: all related issues should go there.' So Zed, the other gpui + alacritty_terminal terminal, has no inline images, and TD would be first in that stack.
bubbles.why: It fills a graphics_mechanism fact for cluster A and confirms TD has no gpui prior art to copy for pixels.

bubbles.note: libghostty-vt, the embeddable VT core extracted from Ghostty (Zig and C API, zero-dependency), now exposes the Kitty graphics protocol to embedders. Ghostling, the minimal libghostty demo terminal (MIT, 1.1k stars), added a full Kitty renderer in PR #13 with 273 lines of C. Ghostel embeds libghostty-vt in Emacs.
bubbles.why: It is a second embeddable core with Kitty graphics besides rio-vt, and a possible candidate subject for cluster A or D. It is not same-stack (Zig, C ABI), but it is the smallest worked example of the embedder's rendering half.

bubbles.note: The Good Image Protocol (Contour, experimental) is the only protocol here designed around compositing layers and named pools. Upload with `DCS u n=<name>,f=<fmt>;!<b64> ST`, render with `DCS r n=<name>,c=<cols>,r=<rows> ST`, release with `DCS d n=<name> ST`. Layers are below, replace and above; the pool uses LRU eviction; it advertises as DA1 code 90. `contour cat` is the reference client. The spec repo has 36 stars and last pushed 2026-04-12, so nobody but Contour has adopted it.
bubbles.why: Named images and explicit layers map neatly onto TD's own 'floating square' idea, but adoption is effectively zero, so it is a design reference, not a protocol to implement.

bubbles.note: kitty's `launch --type=os-panel` creates an OS window 'as a desktop panel' (layer-shell on Wayland). Separately, `--type=overlay` versus `overlay-main` differ in whether the overlay counts as a main window. These are kitty's native equivalents of TD's 'floating square' and 'split pane' targets, reached from open-actions.
bubbles.why: It shows kitty already offers the three destinations TD is designing (overlay over the pane, split, and a panel outside the terminal) behind one launch verb.

bubbles.note: Alacritty's maintainer cited euporie on the day of this run (2026-09-24, issue #910): 'Euporie and its example screenshots are a great example for why I think terminals should not support protocols like Sixel. If your argument for images in terminals is writing GUIs in a terminal, then you're actively working to make terminals and terminal applications worse (imo).'
bubbles.why: This is the strongest current statement of the counter-position to 'GUI in the TUI', aimed at a cluster D subject. It is useful for the brief's 'why not' section.

bubbles.note: I did not research Windows Terminal (Sixel since 1.22 per the brief) or Konsole (Sixel plus Kitty) as subjects. Measured metadata only: microsoft/terminal is MIT, 105.0k stars, C++, latest release v1.24.11911.0 (2026-07-16). I judged both low-value for a Linux, gpui-based TD.
bubbles.why: Explicitly deprioritised by the brief ('only if notable'). Recorded so a later round knows they were considered, not missed.

bubbles.note: Rio's input model (hint and hyperlink bindings) and where_it_draws were not read in docs beyond the features list, so both carry medium confidence. The rioterm.com docs pages for hints and hyperlinks would settle it.
bubbles.why: Only the Rio fields at medium confidence need this follow-up.

I did not read the renderer, so how virtual placements interact with scrollback and alt-screen is unverified. image-storage-limit being separate for primary and alternate screens is measured.
